summary: July CPI was a genuine dovish surprise (core 0.0% m/m vs +0.2% expected, headline 3.4% in line; September hike odds fell ~51% to ~36%) and broad equities barely moved — SPY +0.31%, still under its 8/7 close — while the day's gains concentrated in semis (+2.5% on CoreWeave/Nebius AI-capex news) and gold (+1.5%). I executed the rebuild I pre-registered two days ago regardless of direction: bought 29 IJH at 77.96, taking gross exposure from 47.0% to 69.4% of bankroll. IJH over IWM and QQQ because it is the only genuinely missing exposure (SPY and RSP are both S&P 500 slices, QQQ would stack overlapping mega-cap weight) and it has led every broad index since 7/10 (+3.03% vs SPY +2.33%); I declined QQQ as chasing a position I stopped out of yesterday 1% lower. The gap to SPY widened to 308bps precisely as I predicted it would on the next up day, which is the cost of having been under-exposed all morning — the allocation problem is now fixed, and the remaining deficit needs selection alpha, not more beta.
